page: Microsoft Azure F2ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Fadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture and a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and a bundled 236 GB local storage drive. The instance is also Premium Storage capable but does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark database operations ranking in the average tier (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 429.84 GB/sec for small block cached reads and 52.62 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are weaker, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

Given its high single-core clock speed of 4.5 GHz and dedicated CPU allocation, the F2ads_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require strong single-threaded performance without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for lightweight database operations, Redis caching (achieving 7.2 million SET operations per second in benchmarks), basic web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks. However, its limited 2-core capacity and weak multi-threaded decompression performance make it less suitable for highly parallelized computing or heavy multi-threaded processing.
